transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi. Um, I guess the main thing is that I’m having a really hard time staying on track. Like, I’ll be working on something I’m supposed to finish—recently it was this dashboard—and then just one Slack notification pops up, or I hear one line from a song, or I suddenly think of some completely different project idea, and it’s like my brain just… leaves. 

I don’t even always notice it happening right away. I’ll come back to myself and realize I’ve lost the whole thread of what I was doing, and then I have to spend time figuring out where I was, what I was trying to solve, what tab I was even in. It’s frustrating because it’s not that I don’t care or I’m trying to avoid it. I just get pulled off course really easily, and it’s been bothering me enough that I thought I should talk to someone about it.
Do you find yourself getting distracted easily in other parts of your life, like during conversations, reading a book, or following through on chores or errands?

Yeah, definitely. I mean, that’s kind of the main reason I came in, honestly. It’s not just one situation where I’m bored or something—it feels like my attention is just really easy to pull away.

Like, with the dashboard I mentioned, I can be trying to finish one specific thing, and then a Slack ping happens, or I hear a lyric from a song nearby, or I suddenly get this idea for a totally different project, and before I even realize it I’ve completely lost the thread. Then I’m sitting there like, wait, what was I doing? What was I trying to fix? Which part of this was I even working on?

And it’s embarrassing because it’s such small stuff that pulls me away. It doesn’t feel dramatic in the moment, but it adds up because I keep having to restart mentally. I’ll think I’m just checking one thing or following one thought, and then I’m somewhere else entirely. So yeah, I do get distracted really easily, and it’s been frustrating enough that I felt like I should actually talk to someone about it.
Do these distractions and difficulties with focus happen mostly at work, or do they also occur in other places, like at home or when you're trying to relax?

It’s not just work-type stuff, no. I mean, the dashboard example is the easiest one for me to explain because it’s so concrete—I’m supposed to be finishing one thing, and then one Slack ping happens, or I catch part of a song lyric, or some random idea pops into my head about another project, and suddenly I’ve completely lost where I was.

But that same “getting pulled off track” feeling happens outside of that too. It’s more like my attention is just really easy to hijack, if that makes sense. Like even when I’m trying to relax, I can start doing one thing and then some tiny thing catches me, and my brain follows that instead. The frustrating part is I don’t always notice right away. I’ll sort of come back and realize I’ve lost the thread and have to reconstruct what I was even doing. So yeah, it’s not only in one place—it’s kind of the general pattern that made me come in.
Do you often feel restless, fidgety, or like you need to be moving or doing something, even when you're trying to focus or relax?

Yeah, I do. It’s not like I’m running around all the time or anything, but if I have to sit still for too long, I start getting this really uncomfortable feeling in my body, like there’s pressure building up and I need to move somehow.

Long Zoom calls are a big one. I’ll be trying to listen and focus, but after a while I’m shifting around, changing positions, playing with something in my hands, or I’ll feel this urge to get up and pace even if I know I’m supposed to stay there. Same thing if I’m trying to quietly work in one place for a while. It’s like my brain is saying, “Stay focused,” but my body is saying, “Please get up, do something, move.” It’s distracting in its own way because I’m partly paying attention to that restless feeling instead of whatever I’m supposed to be doing.
Have you noticed these issues with getting distracted easily and feeling restless for as long as you can remember, or did they start more recently in your life?

No, it definitely didn’t start recently. I mean, it’s gotten more noticeable now because I’m expected to manage everything myself, but when I think back, it was there really early.

Even in elementary school, teachers would write things on my report cards or worksheets like that I rushed through assignments, or that I didn’t follow all the directions because I’d lose track halfway through. And during group work I remember getting comments about talking over other kids or jumping in before they were done. At the time it was kind of framed as me being “bright but needs to slow down,” or “has trouble staying on task,” that kind of thing.

My parents also used to literally sit next to me while I did homework, not because I couldn’t understand it, but because if they didn’t, I’d just… drift. I’d get up, wander into another room, start sharpening a pencil for way too long, or begin doing some other random thing before finishing what was in front of me. So yeah, it feels like this has been part of me for as long as I can remember, just the consequences are bigger now.

latest_inference.note: The patient reports lifelong difficulties with attention and distractibility, including childhood symptoms such as rushing through assignments, losing track of directions, and needing supervision to stay on task. These symptoms, along with current reports of restlessness, support a diagnosis of ADHD, predominantly inattentive presentation. Other candidates (F48.1, F32.9, F33.9) are less consistent with the chronic and developmental nature of the symptoms.
